day_shape: 79 items: Trump vows "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran with CENTCOM reporting 65 vessels redirected under Hormuz blockade, IDF strikes Gaza City police station killing 9 and eliminates 4 Nukhba commanders, Israel-Turkey standoff over Syrian Abu al-Duhur airbase deepens, UK minister presses Israel on Gaza aid.

threads.label: Hormuz blockade and Iran sanctions push
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 65 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2 enforcing the blockade, while Trump declared Hormuz "100% successful" and promised the "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran. Axios reported a covert US operation moving ~10 million barrels/day through the strait; Defa Press claimed a US-sanctioned Chinese LPG tanker transited the strait.

threads.label: Israel-Turkey clash over Syrian airbase
threads.summary: Netanyahu said Israel "will not tolerate" Turkish military presence further south in Syria after IAF strikes on Abu al-Duhur airbase, with Chief of Staff Zamir vowing to block hostile forces on Israel's borders. Turkey rejected the allegations; Syria's FM said it had told Israel it was not building a Turkish military presence there; Defa Press framed the strike as a warning to Erdogan.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and IDF operations
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed four Nukhba Force commanders from Hamas's Beit Lahia battalion in Al-Shati and struck a Gaza City police station where Palestinian media reported 9 killed and 15 wounded. The military also announced sealing two Hamas tunnels totalling over 2km and strikes on Hamas commanders in Nuseirat and Tuffah.

threads.label: IDF October 7 probes published
threads.summary: The IDF Military Advocate-General published findings of the first probes since October 7, closing the World Central Kitchen investigation and opening a criminal inquiry into the killing of Hind Rajab. The release covers over 150 probes including Islamic Crescent and other major Gaza cases.

threads.label: UK and European diplomatic activity
threads.summary: UK Minister for the Middle East Stephen Doughty concluded a two-day Egypt visit renewing calls for Israel to allow more aid into Gaza, while Iran International examined a revived European intermediary role in Iran-US diplomacy. The FT reported Iran has weighed attacks on military targets in Europe if Trump escalates.

threads.label: Iran domestic strains and Qalibaf in Iraq
threads.summary: Iran International reported Tehran petrol stations running dry, a new Tehran "moral security" prosecutor's office, a campaign to slaughter 10,000 sheep for Mojtaba Khamenei's health, and Pezeshkian's government opposing an anti-infiltration bill. Speaker Qalibaf visited Baghdad and Kadhimain shrines, telling PM Sudani Iran-Iraq had "unprecedented opportunities" and calling America a source of regional insecurity.

threads.label: Regime-channel military and economic messaging
threads.summary: Defa Press published claims of expanded IRGC missile warhead power via Ansarullah commander Mohbee, air force "forward-looking" lessons from the 12-day and Ramadan wars, a Quincy Institute-attributed US munitions shortage (fewer than 827 Patriot and 278 THAAD interceptors), and record US diesel prices of $5.47/gallon. Yemen's Yahya Saree claimed 9 missile-and-drone operations against Saudi oil facilities and a de facto maritime blockade.

events.title: Two Hamas tunnels, spanning in total some two kilometers underground, were recently sealed by combat engineers, the IDF announces. The IDF says the tunnels were located in central and southern Gaza, amid efforts to clear the Israeli-held portion of the Strip of Hamas infrastructure. The two tunnels were sealed with concrete, the army says. Sealing tunnels with concrete can be a cheaper and less risky alternative to blowing them up, although it takes longer to carry out.
